Level L2, id "guide-first-heading-lines".

runInputs: ["path"].

Hmm — is runInputs required to be non-empty? Not stated. With path input from run, graph_run inputs must include path.

Actually, should I avoid runInputs and just hardcode "GUIDE.md" in instructions? The user said "tell every node that reads to pass exactly the relative path GUIDE.md to read, never an absolute path". Using run input path = "GUIDE.md" is consistent, and instructions say use exactly GUIDE.md relative path. But to be maximally literal, I can set the runInputs path default... there's no default in runInputs. Inputs from run can have fallback? "inputs [{name, from: "run" or a needed node id, field, fallback?}]". So fallback exists. I could set fallback "GUIDE.md" for run inputs. But then graph_run still needs a value for every runInput name. Hmm: "inputs: Object with a value for every name in the plan's runInputs." So I'll pass {"path":"GUIDE.md"}.

Alternative: no runInputs at all, path hardcoded in instructions, and nodes' inputs only from needed nodes. Then anchor has no inputs, exec nodes get path from anchor output. That means anchor output has path "GUIDE.md". That works and avoids runInputs dependency. But does audit require runInputs to be non-empty? Unclear. "runInputs (names)" — probably can be empty.

I think using runInputs ["path"] is cleaner and explicitly gives the relative path. But safest against "fallbacks for inputs from nodes that may fail": inputs from run don't need fallback. Nodes that may fail: anchor mayFail false... exec nodes could fail → verification's inputs from them would need fallback if they mayFail. The check says "fallbacks for inputs from nodes that may fail". If a node has mayFail: true and another consumes its output, fallback required. I'll set mayFail false for exec nodes? But they can fail in reality; mayFail is a declaration. Hmm, if I declare mayFail: false and they do fail, what happens? The run would report failure. Retry budget handles transient.

To be safe: mark execution nodes mayFail: false (read-only deterministic), verification mayFail: false? Verification node with verdict fail is fine. Synthesis mayFail false.

Actually, careful: if a node mayFail: true, the audit warns/rejects missing fallback. Let me just set mayFail false everywhere and rely on retryBudget for retries. Hmm, but is mayFail required? Probably optional, defaulting false.
